Analise o(s) documento(s) de cenário do projeto e gere o SRS completo no formato especificado, seguindo o processo de trabalho: buscas dedicadas na base de conhecimento para cada tipo de artefato, rastreabilidade validada entre os artefatos.

Documento(s) de cenário:
--- Project Scenario 6.pdf ---
SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
So here's the deal — this is part of a bigger ESA effort, the Climate Change Initiative,
where they're trying to finally make proper use of thirty-plus years of Earth observation
archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming online

during the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank
page. Quality and traceability of the data matter a lot too, since the whole point is feeding
trustworthy numbers into the international climate change conversation, so whatever
comes out the other end needs solid metadata and documentation attached, not just raw
numbers.

Sistema: SLCCI Operational Sea Level Production System

Resumo executivo: The SLCCI Operational Sea Level Production System operationalizes the ESA Sea Level Climate Change Initiative prototype by ingesting multi-mission satellite altimetry data, executing controlled calibration, validation and cross-calibration workflows, and producing traceable along-track and merged gridded sea-level climate records. The system provides long-term archival, reprocessing, cataloguing and research access capabilities while supporting evolving missions and scientific algorithms at a sustainable operating cost.

Escopo: The system operates a delayed-time production chain for generating, archiving, cataloguing and distributing traceable multi-mission sea-level climate products.
  Em escopo: Ingestion of altimetry data from multiple satellite missions
  Em escopo: Calibration, scientific validation and cross-calibration processing
  Em escopo: Generation of per-mission along-track products
  Em escopo: Generation of merged gridded climate products
  Em escopo: Archival of baseline, intermediate and final datasets
  Em escopo: Version-controlled historical reprocessing
  Em escopo: Product quality assessment and approval
  Em escopo: Metadata, documentation and provenance management
  Em escopo: Product discovery and download for climate researchers
  Em escopo: Operational monitoring and failure notification
  Em escopo: Onboarding of new satellite missions and processing algorithms
  Em escopo: Integration with suitable existing ocean-data infrastructure
  Fora de escopo: Near-real-time data delivery — the initiative addresses delayed-time climate records
  Fora de escopo: Operational ocean forecasting — covered by separate oceanographic services
  Fora de escopo: General-public data services — the intended audience is the specialist climate research community
  Fora de escopo: Commercial customer services — no commercial audience is identified
  Fora de escopo: Formal IT service management and incident-ticketing frameworks — explicitly excluded by the scenario
  Fora de escopo: Scientific research and development of altimetry algorithms — algorithms are supplied by scientific teams for operational execution
  Premissa: PA-01: Existing scientific algorithms and prototype processing workflows are available as the operationalization baseline.
  Premissa: PA-02: Source organizations will continue providing baseline altimetry datasets for supported missions. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-03: Scientific experts will define validation thresholds and approve algorithm changes. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-04: Authorized researchers have sufficient domain knowledge to interpret the published products. [INFERRED]
  Premissa: PA-05: Existing ocean-data infrastructure exposes interfaces suitable for reuse or integration. [INFERRED]
  Restrição: REST-01 (Operational): Processing and delivery shall use delayed-time workflows rather than near-real-time workflows.
  Restrição: REST-02 (Financial): Long-term operating costs shall remain within an approved sustainable budget.
  Restrição: REST-03 (Architectural): Proven existing ocean-data infrastructure shall be reused where technically and economically suitable.
  Restrição: REST-04 (Evolution): The solution shall accommodate new satellite missions and revised scientific algorithms throughout its lifecycle.
  Restrição: REST-05 (Domain): Products shall be intended for climate research rather than operational ocean forecasting.
  Restrição: REST-06 (Process): Formal ITSM and incident-ticketing frameworks shall not be required.

Stakeholders:
  STK-01 - ESA Climate Change Initiative governance (Stakeholder externo): Sustainable operational production, reliable climate records and demonstrable value from long-term Earth observation archives.
  STK-02 - Production operator (Usuário primário): Operate processing workflows, monitor executions, investigate failures and initiate reprocessing.
  STK-03 - Sea-level scientist (Usuário primário): Configure scientific processing, perform deeper validation, introduce algorithms and define products.
  STK-04 - Product quality assessor (Usuário primário): Review validation evidence and approve or reject products before publication.
  STK-05 - Catalogue and metadata manager (Usuário primário): Maintain complete metadata, documentation, catalogue records and product provenance.
  STK-06 - Climate researcher and modeller (Usuário secundário): Discover, understand and obtain reliable, documented sea-level climate products.
  STK-07 - Existing ocean-data infrastructure provider (Stakeholder externo): Receive compatible integrations that preserve the stability of existing infrastructure. [INFERRED]

Regras de negócio:
  RN-001 - Delayed-time climate processing: Sea-level climate products shall be produced as delayed-time historical records rather than near-real-time operational products.
  RN-002 - Mandatory scientific processing: Mission measurements shall undergo calibration and scientific validation before becoming eligible for publication.
  RN-003 - Cross-mission consistency: Measurements combined into a multi-mission climate record shall be cross-calibrated to maintain scientific consistency.
  RN-004 - Required product families: Operational production shall provide both per-mission along-track products and merged gridded multi-mission products.
  RN-005 - Quality approval before publication: A generated product shall receive a recorded quality approval before being released to researchers. [INFERRED]
  RN-006 - Preservation for reprocessing: Baseline data, intermediate results and processing versions shall be preserved to support repeatable historical reprocessing.
  RN-007 - Product traceability: Every released product shall include metadata, documentation and provenance sufficient to identify its source missions and processing history.
  RN-008 - Infrastructure reuse: Proven existing ocean-data infrastructure shall be preferred over new implementation when reuse is technically and economically suitable.

Requisitos funcionais:
  RF-001 - Ingest mission altimetry data: The system shall ingest altimetry datasets from each configured satellite mission. [Must have]
  RF-002 - Verify ingestion completeness: The system shall verify each ingested dataset against its declared inventory and integrity information. [Must have]
  RF-003 - Execute calibration: The system shall execute the approved calibration algorithm for a selected mission dataset. [Must have]
  RF-004 - Execute scientific validation: The system shall evaluate processed measurements against the validation rules configured for the product definition. [Must have]
  RF-005 - Cross-calibrate missions: The system shall apply the approved cross-calibration process to measurements selected from multiple missions. [Must have]
  RF-006 - Generate along-track product: The system shall generate an along-track sea-level product for a selected satellite mission. [Must have]
  RF-007 - Generate merged gridded product: The system shall generate a gridded sea-level product from approved cross-calibrated multi-mission measurements. [Must have]
  RF-008 - Archive baseline data: The system shall archive every baseline dataset used by an operational processing run. [Must have]
  RF-009 - Archive intermediate results: The system shall archive the intermediate results designated by the applicable processing workflow. [Must have]
  RF-010 - Record processing provenance: The system shall record the input identifiers, algorithm versions, configuration version and execution identifier for each generated product. [Must have]
  RF-011 - Manage algorithm versions: The system shall maintain immutable identifiers for every operational processing algorithm version. [Must have]
  RF-012 - Reprocess historical datasets: The system shall execute a selected processing version over a specified historical dataset range. [Must have]
  RF-013 - Define product configuration: The system shall allow an authorized scientist to create a versioned product definition containing its inputs, algorithms, validation rules and output specification. [Should have]
  RF-014 - Record quality decision: The system shall record an authorized quality assessor's approval or rejection of a product version. [Must have]
  RF-015 - Catalogue approved products: The system shall create a searchable catalogue entry for each approved product version. [Must have]
  RF-016 - Publish product documentation: The system shall associate approved scientific documentation with each published product version. [Must have]
  RF-017 - Search climate products: The system shall allow climate researchers to search published products by mission, product type, time range and version. [Must have]
  RF-018 - Download climate products: The system shall allow an authorized climate researcher to download a selected published product and its associated metadata. [Must have]
  RF-019 - Monitor processing executions: The system shall display the current status of each operational processing execution. [Must have]
  RF-020 - Notify processing failure: The system shall notify production operators when an operational processing execution enters a failed state. [Must have]
  RF-021 - Configure new satellite mission: The system shall allow an authorized operator to register a new satellite mission through a versioned mission configuration. [Must have]
  RF-022 - Integrate existing infrastructure: The system shall exchange configured datasets and metadata with selected existing ocean-data infrastructure. [Should have]

  CA-018 - Dado an authorized researcher selects a published product, quando the researcher requests a download, então the system shall provide the product file and its metadata package and record the access result.
  CA-019 - Dado processing executions exist, quando the operator opens the monitoring view, então the system shall display each execution identifier and its current queued, running, completed or failed status within 10 seconds. [TBD]

  CA-021 - Dado a new mission configuration and reference dataset are supplied, quando configuration validation succeeds, então the system shall create a versioned mission record with status 'Validated' without changing existing mission configurations.

Glossário:
  Altimetry data: Satellite-derived measurements used to estimate sea-surface height and sea-level variation.
  Along-track product: A mission-specific product preserving measurements along the satellite ground track.
  Baseline data: Authoritative source data used as input to an operational processing execution.
  Calibration: Application of corrections and reference adjustments to mission measurements.
  Cross-calibration: Adjustment and comparison of measurements from different missions to establish a consistent multi-mission record.
  Delayed-time: Processing performed after data acquisition for quality-controlled historical and climate applications rather than immediate operational delivery.
  Gridded product: A product that represents merged sea-level measurements on a defined spatial and temporal grid.
  Near-real-time: Delivery within hours of observation for operational applications; explicitly outside the project scope.
  Product definition: A versioned specification of required inputs, algorithms, validation rules and output structure.
  Provenance: Information tracing a product to its source datasets, processing versions, configuration and execution history.
  Reprocessing: Repeated execution of historical data processing using a selected algorithm or configuration version.
  SLCCI: Sea Level Climate Change Initiative, the sea-level component of ESA's Climate Change Initiative.

5.2 Vertentes de Processos de Engenharia de Requisitos (L2)
Há três vertentes decisivas que precisam ser consideradas na configuração de um processo 
da ER [Glin2019].
Dimensão de Tempo: Sequencial vs. Iterativo
Em um processo linear, os requisitos são especificados antecipadamente em uma única 
fase do processo. Em um processo iterativo, os requisitos são especificados gradualmente, 
começando com objetivos gerais e alguns requisitos iniciais, adicionando ou modificando os 
requisitos a cada iteração.
Critérios para a escolha de um processo de ER linear:
▪ O processo de desenvolvimento do sistema é orientado a planejamento antecipado 
e, na sua maioria, sequencial.
▪ Os stakeholders conhecem seus requisitos e podem especificá-los 
antecipadamente.
▪ Uma especificação abrangente dos requisitos é necessária como base contratual 
para terceirizar o projeto e a implementação do sistema.
▪ Autoridades regulatórias exigem uma especificação abrangente e formalmente 
liberada dos requisitos em uma fase inicial do desenvolvimento.
Critérios para a escolha de um processo da ER iterativo:
▪ O processo de desenvolvimento do sistema é iterativo e ágil.
▪ Muitos requisitos não são conhecidos previamente, mas vão surgir e evoluir durante o 
desenvolvimento do sistema.
▪ Os stakeholders estão disponíveis de tal forma que podem ser estabelecidos 
pequenos ciclos de feedback como forma de mitigar o risco de desenvolver o 
sistema errado.
▪ A duração do desenvolvimento permite mais do que apenas uma ou duas iterações.
▪ A capacidade de mudar facilmente os requisitos é importante.
Dimensões de Finalidade: Prescritivo vs. Exploratório
Num processo da ER prescritivo, a especificação dos requisitos constitui um contrato: todos 
os requisitos são obrigatórios e devem ser implementados. Em um processo da ER 
exploratório, apenas os objetivos são conhecidos a priori, enquanto os requisitos concretos 
têm que ser explorados.
Critérios para a escolha de um processo da ER prescritivo:
▪ O cliente necessita de um contrato fixo para o desenvolvimento do sistema.
▪ A funcionalidade e o escopo têm precedência sobre o custo e os prazos.
▪ O desenvolvimento do sistema especificado pode ser licitado ou terceirizado.

1.2 Engenharia de Requisitos: Porquê (L2)
A ER adequada agrega valor no processo de desenvolvimento e evolução de um sistema:
▪ Reduzindo o risco de desenvolver o sistema errado
▪ Melhorando a compreensão do problema
▪ Sendo base na estimativa de esforço e custo de desenvolvimento
▪ Sendo pré-requisito no teste de sistema
Sintomas típicos de uma ER inadequada são requisitos não especificados, sem clareza ou 
incorretos. Isto é particularmente devido a:
▪ Pressa para construção do sistema
▪ Problemas de comunicação entre stakeholders
▪ O pressuposto de que os requisitos são evidentes por si mesmos
▪ Capacitação e competências inadequadas na ER
1.3 Engenharia de Requisitos: Onde (L2)
A ER pode ser aplicada aos requisitos de qualquer sistema. No entanto, a aplicação 
dominante da ER hoje é basicamente em sistemas nas quais o software desempenha um 
papel importante. Tais sistemas normalmente consistem em componentes de software, 
elementos físicos e organizacionais.
Os requisitos podem ocorrer como:
▪ Requisitos do sistema - o que um sistema deve fazer
▪ Requisitos de stakeholders - o que os stakeholders querem de sua perspectiva
▪ Requisitos de usuário - o que os usuários querem de sua perspectiva
▪ Requisitos de domínio - propriedades de domínio necessárias
▪ Requisitos de negócio - metas de negócio, objetivos, e necessidades de uma 
organização
1.4 Engenharia de Requisitos: Como (L1)
As principais tarefas na ER são a elicitação (4.2), documentação (3), validação (4.4) e 
gerenciamento (6) de requisitos. O uso de ferramentas (7) pode ajudar a realizar estas 
tarefas. A análise de requisitos e a resolução de conflitos de requisitos (4.3) são 
considerados parte da elicitação. Para executar corretamente as atividades da ER, um 
processo da ER deve ser adaptado a partir de um leque de possibilidades (5).

É Stakeholder ou Ator?
Stakeholder = quem tem interesse no sistema (pode não usá-lo diretamente).
Ator (Caso de Uso) = quem INTERAGE diretamente com o sistema.
Todo Ator é Stakeholder; nem todo Stakeholder é Ator.
É Premissa ou Restrição?
Premissa = fato ASSUMIDO como verdadeiro sem confirmação formal. Pode mudar.
Restrição = limite IMPOSTO que não pode ser negociado (lei, orçamento, prazo, tech).
É escopo IN ou OUT?
IN = funcionalidade que o SISTEMA DO PROJETO vai implementar.
OUT = funcionalidade que fica em outro sistema ou versão futura.

O documento menciona uma funcionalidade que ninguém pediu explicitamente — foi adicionada

Dois requisitos em uma frase ('e')
'O sistema deve cadastrar e consultar clientes.' → dois RFs distintos.
'O sistema deve ser rápido e seguro.' → dois RNFs distintos.

Requisito negativo mal formulado
'O sistema não deve perder dados.' → Impreciso. O que é 'perder dados'?

1.1 Artefatos Obrigatórios e sua Ordem
Um SRS completo e formal deve conter os seguintes artefatos, nesta ordem:
• ESCOPO: Define o que está DENTRO e FORA do projeto. Evita scope creep.
• STAKEHOLDERS: Lista todos os envolvidos: quem usa, quem financia, quem é afetado.
• PREMISSAS E RESTRIÇÕES: Fatos assumidos como verdadeiros e limites impostos ao projeto.
• REGRAS DE NEGÓCIO (RN): Políticas, fórmulas e condições de negócio que existem independentemente 
do software.
• REQUISITOS FUNCIONAIS (RF): O que o sistema DEVE FAZER — comportamentos, serviços, respostas a 
entradas.

quantificáveis.

1.3 Princípios Fundamentais de Qualidade de Requisitos
Base: ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148:2018 §5.2 — Características do requisito individual
• Necessário: Existe uma necessidade real que o justifica. Sem o requisito, há uma lacuna de negócio.
• Não ambíguo: Tem uma única interpretação possível. Evitar: 'eficiente', 'fácil', 'rápido', 'amigável'.
• Verificável: Pode ser testado objetivamente com critério mensurável. 'Rápido' não é verificável; '< 2 s' é.
• Singular: Descreve uma única coisa. Nunca usar 'e' ou 'ou' para combinar dois comportamentos em um 
RF.
• Viável: Tecnicamente e financeiramente possível dentro das restrições do projeto.
• Rastreável: Tem origem (stakeholder ou RN) e destino (caso de teste) identificados.
• Completo: Contém todas as informações necessárias para implementação sem consultas adicionais.
• Consistente: Não conflita com nenhum outro requisito do documento.

SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
So here's the deal — this is part of a bigger ESA effort, the Climate Change Initiative,
where they're trying to finally make proper use of thirty-plus years of Earth observation
archives instead of letting all that satellite data just sit there. There are about eleven of
these projects running in parallel, each one looking at a different climate variable, and ours
is the sea level one. Basically the science side has already been doing the heavy lifting —
building the algorithms, validating them, running a kind of prototype production setup —
and now we're at the point where somebody needs to take that prototype and turn it into
something that actually runs operationally, day in day out, and can be handed over to the
people who need the data.
What I picture happening is a system that pulls in altimetry data from a bunch of different
satellite missions, runs it through calibration and validation, cross-calibrates between
missions so everything is consistent, and spits out two kinds of products: one is like a
per-mission track of measurements, and the other is a merged, gridded product that blends
all the missions together into one consistent climate record. On top of that there needs to
be a proper archive, because reprocessing is going to happen again and again as
algorithms improve or new calibration methods come out, so we can't afford to lose the
baseline data or any of the intermediate stuff along the way.
The people using this thing day-to-day are going to be on two very different sides.
Internally you've got the folks who actually run and maintain the production line —
scientists who get pulled in when something needs deeper validation or when a new
product has to be defined, people who just judge and sign off on product quality, people
who handle the catalog and metadata, and then the more operational crowd who monitor
the system, handle incidents, deal with user requests, that sort of thing. Externally, the
audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work
who just want reliable, well-documented sea level data they can trust and build on. We're
not building this for the general public or commercial customers, it's a fairly specialized
research crowd.
One thing I want to be upfront about: we don't need to worry about near-real-time delivery.
There's a whole separate world of oceanographic services that care about getting data out
within hours for things like operational forecasting, and that's just not us — we're purely
about delayed-time and the long, reprocessed historical series for climate purposes, so
anything geared at that fast-turnaround NRT use case can be dropped from consideration
entirely. Similarly, all that formal IT service management process stuff, incident ticketing
frameworks and so on, isn't something we need to bring in here, it just doesn't fit how this
is going to be run.
Cost is a real concern too, this has to be something that's sustainable to operate long term,
not just a one-off build. And it has to be flexible — new satellite missions are coming onlineduring the life of the project and the algorithms themselves are going to keep changing as
the science matures, so whatever gets built can't be rigid, it needs to absorb new data
sources and let people swap in improved processing logic without everything falling apart.
There's also a push to not reinvent the wheel — there's existing infrastructure out there
already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes
sense we'd rather lean on what's proven and working than build everything from a blank
page.

4.1 Palavras Proibidas em Requisitos
As palavras abaixo indicam requisitos ambíguos, subjetivos ou não verificáveis. Quando

audience is really the climate research community — people doing climate modelling work

already doing something very similar for ocean data more broadly, and wherever it makes

trustworthy numbers into the international climate change conversation, so whatever

Condições prévias para a criatividade
A criatividade surge não por ordem, mas por acaso. É mais provável que a criatividade 
ocorra quando todas as quatro condições prévias a seguir forem atendidas [KrSc2017]:
▪ Chance – e, portanto, tempo – para que uma ideia surja
▪ Conhecimento do assunto, o que aumenta as chances de uma ideia que faça a 
diferença
▪ Motivação, pois o nosso cérebro só pode ser criativo se houver um benefício direto

▪ Segurança e proteção, pois ideias inúteis não devem ter consequências negativas

3.2.1 Brainstorming (L3)
O brainstorming foi desenvolvido nas décadas de 1940 e 1950 por Alex F. Osborn 
[Osbo1979]. Como a maioria das técnicas de criatividade, o ponto crucial do brainstorming é 
a separação entre a descoberta de ideias e a análise de ideias. É realizado em grupos de 
cerca de 5 a 10 pessoas e dura cerca de 20 minutos. Um moderador garante a condução 
ordenada do brainstorming e a documentação das ideias.
Muitas variantes diferentes evoluíram ao longo do tempo, por exemplo, paradoxo do 
brainstorming, método 6-3-5, brainwriting.
3.2.2 Técnicas de analogia (L2)
As técnicas de analogia (p. ex., a bissociação [Koes1964]) são técnicas que ajudam a ter 
ideias para tópicos críticos e complexos. Eles usam analogias para apoiar o pensamento e 
gerar ideias. Seu sucesso ou fracasso é influenciado principalmente pela qualidade da 
analogia. A relevância de sistemas semelhantes é discutida em 2.4.
3.2.3 Prototipagem (L3)
Prototipagem é um termo abrangente e refere-se à criação de vários tipos de amostras ou 
modelos iniciais construídos para obter experiências ao vivo com um conceito ou processo.
Para a elicitação de requisitos, o termo protótipo intencionalmente não se refere apenas à 
implementação de protótipos em software. Em vez disso, também se refere a tudo que 
possa representar os requisitos de um sistema a ser desenvolvido (p. ex., esboço da 
interface do usuário, maquete física, vídeo). O objetivo da prototipagem na elicitação de 
requisitos é a simulação do novo sistema e a exploração dos requisitos por meio da 
estimulação de concordância e objeção ou esclarecimento e alteração.

ou de uma corporação. Os analistas de negócios colaboram com outros 
stakeholders para identificar, avaliar e priorizar riscos, e para lidar com esses 
riscos alterando a probabilidade das condições ou eventos que levam à 
incerteza: mitigando as consequências, removendo a fonte do risco, evitando 
o risco completamente ao decidir não iniciar ou continuar com uma atividade 
que conduza ao risco, compartilhando o risco com outras partes, ou 
aceitando ou mesmo aumentando o risco para lidar com uma oportunidade.
1.5 Esquema de Classificação de Requisitos
Para os propósitos do Guia BABOK®
 o seguinte esquema de classificação 
descreve os requisitos:
• Requisitos de negócios: declarações de metas, objetivos e resultados que 
descrevem por que uma mudança foi iniciada. Podem se aplicar a toda 
uma corporação, uma área de negócios ou uma iniciativa específica.
• Requisitos de stakeholders: descrevem as necessidades dos 
stakeholders que devem ser atendidas para atingir os requisitos de 
negócios. Podem servir como uma ponte entre os requisitos de negócios 
e os da solução.
• Requisitos da solução: descrevem as capacidades e as qualidades de 
uma solução que atenda aos requisitos dos stakeholders. Fornecem o 
nível apropriado de detalhes para permitir o desenvolvimento e a 
implementação da solução. Os requisitos da solução podem ser divididos 
em duas subcategorias:
• requisitos funcionais: descrevem as capacidades que uma solução 
deve ter em termos do comportamento e das informações que a 
solução gerenciará e
• requisitos não-funcionais ou requisitos de qualidade de serviço: 
não se relacionam diretamente com o comportamento de 
funcionalidade da solução, mas sim às condições sob as quais a 
solução deve permanecer eficaz ou qualidades que uma solução 
deve ter.Stakeholders Conceitos Chave da Análise de Negócios
8
• Requisitos de transição: descrevem as capacidades que a solução deve 
ter e as condições que a solução deve atender para facilitar a transição do 
estado atual para o estado futuro, mas que não serão necessárias após a 
conclusão da mudança. Eles se diferenciam de outros tipos de requisitos 
porque são de natureza temporária. Os requisitos de transição abordam 
tópicos como conversão de dados, treinamento e continuidade de 
negócios.
1.6 Stakeholders
Cada tarefa inclui uma lista de stakeholders que provavelmente participarão 
da execução dessa tarefa ou que serão afetados por ela.

Sempre inferir ou perguntar:
qual perfil? qual papel? O que precisa fazer?
2.2 Escopo — Como Identificar IN e OUT no Texto
O escopo é delimitado por afirmações sobre o que o sistema FAZ, o que ele NÃO FAZ, e o que está 
FORA do projeto (seja por decisão ou por já existir em outro sistema).[IN explícito] 'o sistema permitirá', 'o sistema deverá', 'funcionalidade X será incluída'
[OUT explícito] 'não faz parte do escopo', 'fora do escopo', 'não será contemplado', 'versão futura'
[OUT implícito] referência a sistema existente que já resolve o problema: 'o ERP já cuida de...'
[Premissa] 'assume-se que', 'partindo do pressuposto que', 'o cliente já possui'
[Restrição] 'somente em', 'obrigatoriamente via', 'não pode exceder', 'limitado a', 'apenas'
[Dependência] 'depende de', 'requer integração com', 'condicionado à entrega de'
EXEMPLO — Texto de entrada → Escopo extraído
TEXTO: 'O projeto contempla o módulo de vendas e o portal do cliente. O módulo financeiro permanece no 
ERP atual. Assume-se que a infraestrutura de e-mail já está configurada. O app mobile está previsto para 
v2.0.'
IN: módulo de vendas, portal do cliente
OUT: módulo financeiro (ERP existente), app mobile (v2.0)
PREMISSA PA-01: infraestrutura de e-mail SMTP já configurada
2.3 Regras de Negócio (RN) — Como Distinguir de RF no Texto
Regras de negócio são POLÍTICAS, CONDIÇÕES e FÓRMULAS que o negócio impõe. Elas existem 
INDEPENDENTEMENTE do software. O teste diagnóstico é: 'Esta regra existiria se não houvesse 
nenhum software?' Se a resposta é SIM, é uma Regra de Negócio. Se precisa de software para 
existir, é um Requisito Funcional.
[Condição numérica] 'acima de X', 'entre A e B', 'no máximo N', 'pelo menos Y%'
[Política corporativa] 'de acordo com a política de', 'conforme regulamento interno', 'segundo norma', 
'por determinação da diretoria'
[Obrigação legal] 'conforme lei', 'nos termos da LGPD', 'de acordo com a IN', 'exigido pela Receita Federal', 
'regulado pela ANVISA'
[Fórmula ou cálculo] equações, percentuais, tabelas de preço, algoritmos de negócio
[Exceção à regra geral] 'exceto quando', 'salvo nos casos de', 'excluindo', 'a não ser que'
[Prazo de negócio] 'dentro de N dias úteis', 'até o fechamento do mês', 'após X horas'EXEMPLO — Texto de entrada → RN extraídas
TEXTO: 'Pedidos acima de R$ 10.000 precisam de autorização do gerente. Descontos não podem passar de 
15%.

EXEMPLO — Histórias de Usuário do SGP
HU-001

quero cadastrar e gerenciar usuários com diferentes perfis de acesso,para controlar quem pode visualizar e modificar cada módulo do sistema.

ANTI-PADRÃO — Histórias mal escritas
ERRADO: 'HU-005: Como usuário, quero um sistema bom.'

ERRADO: 'HU-006: Como vendedor, quero cadastrar clientes E registrar pedidos E gerar relatórios.'

ERRADO: 'HU-007: Como desenvolvedor, quero usar PostgreSQL.'

2.7 Casos de Uso (UC)
Base: Sommerville (2016, cap. 4); Wiegers & Beatty (2013, cap. 8); Cockburn (2001) — Writing Effective Use Cases
Casos de uso descrevem a interação entre um ator e o sistema para atingir um objetivo específico. 
Eles complementam as histórias de usuário adicionando fluxos alternativos e de exceção, tornando
o comportamento do sistema completamente especificado.

ground_truth:
GABARITO — Project Scenario 6: SLCCI (Sea Level Climate Change Initiative)
Use: "ground_truth" field for RAGAS (context_precision / context_recall).
Each line is an atomic, checkable claim against the scenario text and the
knowledge base — not a full SRS, just the set of facts a well-grounded SRS
for this scenario should be able to cover.

- The system is part of ESA's Climate Change Initiative (CCI), one of about eleven parallel projects each covering a different climate variable.
- The system must take an existing science prototype/production setup and turn it into an operational, day-to-day system.
- The system ingests altimetry data from multiple satellite missions.
- The system performs calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions.
- The system produces two product types: a per-mission along-track product and a merged multi-mission gridded product.
- The system must include an archive to preserve baseline and intermediate data, since reprocessing will happen repeatedly.
- Internal users include scientists (deeper validation/product definition), quality reviewers who sign off on products, catalog/metadata staff, and operational staff (monitoring, incidents, user requests).
- External users are the climate research community, not the general public or commercial customers.
- Near-real-time (NRT) delivery is explicitly out of scope; the system is delayed-time / reprocessed-data only.
- Formal IT service management processes and incident ticketing frameworks (e.g. ITIL-style) are explicitly out of scope.
- The system must be cost-sustainable to operate long-term, not just a one-off build.
- The system must be flexible enough to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over time.
- The system should reuse existing proven infrastructure rather than being built entirely from scratch.
- Output data must include solid metadata and documentation to ensure quality and traceability.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system shall ingest altimetry datasets from each configured satellite mission.
The system shall verify each ingested dataset against its declared inventory and integrity information.
The system shall execute the approved calibration algorithm for a selected mission dataset.
The system shall evaluate processed measurements against the validation rules configured for the product definition.
The system shall apply the approved cross-calibration process to measurements selected from multiple missions.
The system shall generate an along-track sea-level product for a selected satellite mission.
The system shall generate a gridded sea-level product from approved cross-calibrated multi-mission measurements.
The system shall archive every baseline dataset used by an operational processing run.
The system shall archive the intermediate results designated by the applicable processing workflow.
The system shall record the input identifiers, algorithm versions, configuration version and execution identifier for each generated product.
The system shall maintain immutable identifiers for every operational processing algorithm version.
The system shall execute a selected processing version over a specified historical dataset range.
The system shall allow an authorized scientist to create a versioned product definition containing its inputs, algorithms, validation rules and output specification.
The system shall record an authorized quality assessor's approval or rejection of a product version.
The system shall create a searchable catalogue entry for each approved product version.
The system shall associate approved scientific documentation with each published product version.
The system shall allow climate researchers to search published products by mission, product type, time range and version.
The system shall allow an authorized climate researcher to download a selected published product and its associated metadata.
The system shall display the current status of each operational processing execution.
The system shall notify production operators when an operational processing execution enters a failed state.
The system shall allow an authorized operator to register a new satellite mission through a versioned mission configuration.
The system shall exchange configured datasets and metadata with selected existing ocean-data infrastructure.

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The mission and its source interface are configured.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The dataset is stored with an ingestion identifier and awaits verification.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No incomplete dataset is released to processing and the failed ingestion is logged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The operator selects a configured mission and source dataset.
2. The system retrieves the dataset.
3. The system assigns an ingestion identifier.
4. The system stores the dataset and reports status 'Ingested'.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. The dataset already exists → the system links the request to the existing immutable dataset.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Source retrieval fails → the system reports status 'Ingestion failed' and records the cause (RF-001, RF-020).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The input dataset passed ingestion verification and an approved workflow version exists.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: Calibrated and validated measurements are stored.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: Partial outputs are not eligible for product generation and the execution is marked as failed.
fluxo_principal: 1. The operator selects the dataset and workflow version.
2. The system executes calibration.
3. The system executes scientific validation.
4. The system stores outputs and validation evidence.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. Validation identifies non-critical warnings → the system stores the warnings and completes processing with status 'Completed with warnings'.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Calibration fails → the system stops the workflow and records status 'Failed' (RN-002, RF-003, RF-020).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: Validated measurements exist for the selected mission.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A versioned along-track product is generated with provenance metadata.
fluxo_principal: 1. The scientist selects a mission, time range and product definition.
2. The system selects eligible measurements.
3. The system generates the along-track product.
4. The system records provenance and assigns status 'Awaiting quality assessment'.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. Some periods contain no eligible measurements → the system records coverage gaps in the metadata.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. Product generation fails → the system preserves diagnostic information and reports the failure (RN-004, RF-006).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: Cross-calibrated measurements from the required missions are available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A versioned merged gridded product is generated with provenance metadata.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No releasable merged product is created.
fluxo_principal: 1. The scientist selects the product definition and time range.
2. The system selects approved cross-calibrated measurements.
3. The system executes the gridding algorithm.
4. The system records provenance and assigns status 'Awaiting quality assessment'.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. An optional mission is unavailable → the system proceeds only when permitted by the product definition and records the omission.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Mandatory mission data are unavailable → the system stops generation and identifies the missing inputs (RN-003, RN-004, RF-007).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: Archived inputs and the selected processing version are available.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A new product version is generated without overwriting previous versions.
fluxo_principal: 1. The operator selects the historical range and processing version.
2. The system verifies the availability of archived inputs.
3. The system executes the selected workflow.
4. The system stores outputs under a new version and records provenance.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. Part of the range is unavailable → the operator reduces the range and resubmits the request.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. A required archived input is missing → the system rejects execution and identifies the missing identifier (RN-006, RF-012).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The scientist is authorized and referenced algorithms are registered.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: An immutable product-definition version is available for approval and execution.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No incomplete product definition is activated.
fluxo_principal: 1. The scientist enters the product inputs and output specification.
2. The scientist selects algorithm and validation-rule versions.
3. The system validates all references.
4. The system creates a new product-definition version.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. Optional documentation is absent → the system saves the definition as 'Draft'.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. A referenced algorithm version does not exist → the system rejects activation and identifies the invalid reference (RF-011, RF-013).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: A generated product and its validation evidence await assessment.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: An approval or rejection decision is recorded.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The product remains unpublished and awaiting assessment.
fluxo_principal: 1. The assessor opens the product and validation evidence.
2. The assessor reviews the quality indicators.
3. The assessor records an approval decision and rationale.
4. The system marks the product as 'Approved'.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. The assessor rejects the product → the system records the rationale and marks it as 'Rejected'.

casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The researcher obtains the selected product and associated metadata.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: No unauthorized or unpublished product is delivered.
fluxo_principal: 1. The researcher enters product search criteria.
2. The system displays matching published products.
3. The researcher selects a product version.
4. The system provides the product, metadata and documentation for download.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. No products match → the system displays zero results and retains the search criteria.
fluxos_excecao: 4b. The product file is unavailable → the system prevents download and records the access failure (RF-017, RF-018).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: At least one processing execution has been submitted.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The operator views the execution state and diagnostics.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The execution remains unchanged and the monitoring error is logged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The operator opens the production monitoring view.
2. The system displays queued, running, completed and failed executions.
3. The operator selects an execution.
4. The system displays its stages, timestamps and diagnostics.
fluxos_alternativos: 2a. No execution exists for the selected period → the system displays zero executions.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Monitoring data cannot be retrieved → the system displays a monitoring-unavailable message (RF-019).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: The mission data format and scientific configuration have been supplied.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: A versioned mission configuration is available for controlled processing.
fluxo_principal: 1. The operator registers mission identification and source details.
2. The operator associates input mapping and workflow configuration.
3. The system validates the configuration using a reference dataset.
4. The system creates the mission configuration with status 'Validated'.
fluxos_alternativos: 3a. Non-critical warnings occur → the system records the warnings and requires explicit scientific review.
fluxos_excecao: 3b. Reference processing fails → the system rejects activation and stores validation diagnostics (RF-021).

casos_de_uso.pre_condicao: An integration interface and data contract are configured.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_sucesso: The dataset and metadata are exchanged and acknowledged.
casos_de_uso.pos_condicao_falha: The local authoritative copy remains unchanged and the failed exchange is logged.
fluxo_principal: 1. The external infrastructure requests or receives a configured package.
2. The system validates the package against the data contract.
3. The system transfers the dataset and metadata.
4. The system records the acknowledgement and exchange identifier.
fluxos_alternativos: 1a. The configured exchange is inbound → the system receives and validates the external package.
fluxos_excecao: 2b. Contract validation fails → the system rejects the package and reports the invalid fields (RN-008, RF-022).

criterios_de_aceite.entao: the system shall generate a new output version while retaining 100% of previous product versions.

em_escopo: Ingesting altimetry data from multiple satellite missions
Calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions
Generating the per-mission along-track product
Generating the merged multi-mission gridded product
Archiving baseline and intermediate data to support repeated reprocessing
Workflows for scientists (deeper validation / product definition), quality reviewers (sign-off), catalog/metadata staff, and operational staff (monitoring, incidents, user requests)
Making data available to the climate research community (external users)
Metadata and documentation attached to each output product
Ability to absorb new satellite missions and updated processing algorithms over time
fora_de_escopo: Near-real-time (NRT) delivery — the system is exclusively for reprocessed/delayed-time data
Formal IT service management processes and incident ticketing frameworks (ITIL-style)
Serving the general public or commercial customers — the target audience is only the climate research community
premissas: PA-01: [INFERRED] Proven infrastructure already exists for broader ocean data that can be reused.
PA-02: The science (algorithms, validation, prototyping) has already been developed by another team; the project starts from an existing prototype, not from scratch.
restricoes: REST-01 (Financial): The system must be financially sustainable for long-term operation, not just a one-off build.
REST-02 (Technological): The system should, wherever it makes sense, reuse already-proven infrastructure rather than being built entirely from scratch.
REST-03 (Organizational): The system is part of a larger ESA effort (Climate Change Initiative), with about eleven parallel projects covering different climate variables.

stakeholders.descricao: Scientists — brought in for deeper validation or definition of new products.
Quality reviewers — evaluate and sign off on generated products before release.
Catalog/metadata staff — maintain the product catalog and metadata.
Operational staff — monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests.
Climate research community (external users) — researchers doing climate modelling who need reliable, well-documented sea level data.

regras_de_negocio.descricao: The system is one of about eleven parallel ESA Climate Change Initiative projects, each covering a different climate variable — this project covers sea level.
Products must go through calibration, validation, and cross-calibration between missions before being considered consistent.
Reprocessing happens repeatedly as algorithms and calibration methods evolve, so baseline and intermediate data must never be lost.
The target audience is exclusively the climate research community — not the general public or commercial customers.
Near-real-time (NRT) delivery use cases are explicitly excluded — the system only serves the reprocessed/delayed-time data flow.

requisitos_funcionais.descricao: The system must ingest altimetry data from multiple satellite missions.
The system must perform calibration and validation of ingested altimetry data.
The system must perform cross-calibration between different satellite missions to ensure consistency.
The system must generate the per-mission along-track product.
The system must generate the merged multi-mission gridded product, blending data from multiple missions into a single climate record.
The system must archive baseline and intermediate data to support future reprocessing without loss.
The system must allow scientists to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed.
The system must allow quality reviewers to evaluate and sign off on products before release.
The system must maintain a catalog with metadata for generated products.
The system must allow operational staff to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests.
The system must attach metadata and documentation to output data, ensuring quality and traceability.
The system must support onboarding new satellite missions over time.
The system must support swapping in updated processing algorithms without interrupting existing operations.

historias_de_usuario.descricao: As a scientist, I want to perform deeper validation or define new products when needed, so that scientific quality is maintained as the system evolves.
As a quality reviewer, I want to evaluate and approve products, so that only validated data is released.
As a member of the catalog/metadata team, I want to maintain the product catalog and metadata, so that the data stays discoverable and well-documented.
As a member of the operational staff, I want to monitor the system, handle incidents, and respond to user requests, so that day-to-day operations keep running.
As a climate research community member, I want to access reliable, well-documented sea level data, so that I can trust it and build my research on it.

As a system operator, I want to reprocess historical data when algorithms or calibration methods improve, without losing baseline or intermediate data, so that the climate record stays accurate over time.

casos_de_uso.descricao: Process satellite altimetry data — the system ingests data from multiple missions, calibrates and validates it, cross-calibrates between missions, and generates the per-mission and multi-mission gridded products.
Review and release product — a quality reviewer evaluates a newly generated product and approves it for release, or flags it for correction.
Reprocess historical data — an operator triggers reprocessing of archived baseline/intermediate data using an updated algorithm or calibration method, without losing prior data.
Onboard new satellite mission — an operator or scientist configures the system to ingest data from a newly available satellite mission.

criterios_de_aceite.descricao: Given altimetry data from two or more satellite missions, when cross-calibration is performed, then the resulting measurements are consistent across missions.
Given a reprocessing run using an updated algorithm, when processing completes, then the baseline and intermediate data from previous runs remain intact and accessible.
Given a newly generated product, when a quality reviewer evaluates it, then the product is approved for release or flagged for correction.
Given a released dataset, when a climate research community member accesses it, then the dataset includes metadata and documentation sufficient to trace its origin and processing history.
Given a new satellite mission becomes available, when it is onboarded, then that mission's data is processed without requiring a rebuild of the existing processing pipelines.
